divergences.old: jenkins instance add --name --base-url [--username] [--api-token] [--force] and jenkins instance remove --name, editing the jenkinsInstances array in the global config
divergences.toil: A named instance is a jenkins connection. jenkins instance add <name> is toil connections add <name> --area jenkins: it takes the name as an argument, asks for baseUrl, username, instance and the API token on a terminal, and keeps the token in the OS credential store. jenkins instance remove <name> is toil connections remove <name> --area jenkins, which also deletes the token from the store and refuses a connection to another area. Both are CLI only, take the name as an argument instead of --name, return the connections commands' data, and the contract's other flags aren't accepted
divergences.why: Only the toil connections commands write config, and a secret goes only to the OS credential store or an env var, never into a config file from a flag. Core answers all three instance commands, so the jenkins area never receives the whole config or the credential store.

divergences.old: jenkins --instance <name> picking an entry of jenkinsInstances, with "Jenkins instance \"<name>\" not found" for an unknown name and "has no baseUrl configured" for an entry without one
divergences.toil: --instance (or the MCP instance field) selects a jenkins connection, by its name or by its instance setting. An unknown name is INVALID_INPUT listing the instances toil knows; a connection without baseUrl, username or apiToken is refused when it's resolved, with the usual fix. A connection also takes shared settings from defaults.jenkins, and TOIL_JENKINS_* env vars apply to the default connection only
divergences.why: Config is a set of named connections, and --instance is a context input that selects one, resolved by core in the same order for every area.

divergences.old: jenkins instance list returning { instances: [{ name, baseUrl, username, apiToken: "***" }] } for the jenkinsInstances entries only
divergences.toil: It is toil connections list --area jenkins: every jenkins connection, the default one included, as { configFile, connections: [{ name, area, isDefault, host, writes, values }] }, where values says where each setting came from and never holds a secret
divergences.why: Core answers it, so the jenkins area never receives the whole config or the credential store; every jenkins connection is an instance --instance can select.

divergences.old: jenkins pipeline run --wait returning the build as a success envelope and exiting 1 when the build's result is set and not SUCCESS
divergences.toil: The same: ok, the build as data, and exit code 1. toil adds a JENKINS_BUILD_NOT_SUCCESSFUL warning in meta.warnings naming the build and its result
divergences.why: The warning is additive output the contract allows, and it makes the failure visible to MCP callers, who never see an exit code.

divergences.old: jenkins pipeline run --wait waiting as long as --timeout allowed, twice
divergences.toil: The command's time limit is 21 minutes: two default 600 s phases and a minute of polling. A longer --timeout ends in TIMEOUT at that limit unless TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS raises it
divergences.why: Every command has a time limit and can be cancelled; one that waits on slow work declares a longer limit, not none.

divergences.old: jenkins pipeline run and run logs failing on the first HTTP 429, and logging progress lines ("Queued build", "Waiting for build to start") to stderr
divergences.toil: A 429 is retried up to three times, as it is for every request toil sends, and the progress lines go to stderr only with --debug
divergences.why: Every request goes through the one HTTP path areas share, and a command has no channel to stderr but --debug.
